items.stem: Explain three features of the parliamentary system in India.
items.answer: (1) The President is the nominal head and the Prime Minister the real head. (2) Ministers are members of Parliament. (3) The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. (4) The government can be removed by a no-confidence motion.

items.stem: Evaluate one advantage and one disadvantage of the parliamentary system for a diverse country like India.
items.answer: (1) Advantage: different regions and groups are represented in the government. (2) Advantage: the government is answerable daily to Parliament. (3) Disadvantage: coalition governments may be unstable. (4) Disadvantage: decisions can be slowed by debates and party politics.

items.stem:
(a) Why does India need two houses of Parliament? Analyse. (3 marks)
(b) Why is the Rajya Sabha called a permanent house? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) The Lok Sabha represents the people directly. (2) The Rajya Sabha represents the states and supports federalism. (3) The second house gives time for careful review of bills. (4) Nominated members bring expertise in art, science, literature and social service. (b) (1) It is never dissolved as a whole. (2) Only one-third of its members retire every two years.

(b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) It is never dissolved as a whole. (2) Only one-third of its members retire every two years.

items.stem:
(a) What happens if the Lok Sabha passes an ordinary bill but the Rajya Sabha rejects it? (3 marks)
(b) Why is a bill discussed in stages (readings) before it becomes a law? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) There is a deadlock between the houses. (2) The President may call a joint sitting. (3) The bill is decided by a majority of members of both houses present, so the larger Lok Sabha usually prevails. (b) (1) Members can debate and improve it. (2) Committees can study it in detail and suggest changes.
